articles.title: Why has Shafali Verma been reprimanded by the ICC after India's win over Zimbabwe?
articles.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the
articles.body: India vice-captain Shafali Verma has received an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe.The incident took place during India's nine-wicket win in Raipur on Sunday. The 22-year-old was found guilty of breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct.What happened during the match?The incident took place in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings. Shafali dropped a catch offered by Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling. She then threw the ball to the ground in frustration.The ICC found that Shafali had breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel. This rule deals with the “abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match,” an ICC media release said.One demerit point added to her recordAlong with the official reprimand, one demerit point has been added to Shafali's disciplinary record. This was her first offence in a 24-month period.Shafali admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by G.S. Lakshmi of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees. As a result, there was no need for a formal hearing.On-field umpires Vrinda Rathi and Gayathri Venugopalan, third umpire Anna Harris and fourth umpire Janani Narayanan levelled the charge.What is the penalty for a Level 1 breach?Level 1 breaches of the ICC Code of Conduct carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand. articles.title: ICC T20I Rankings: Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma dominate as Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud make gains
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s dominance in the ICC Women’s T20I Bowling Rankings continues, with Shree Charani and Deepti Sharma retaining the top two positions, while fast bowlers Nandani Sharma and Kranti Gaud made significant gains following the ongoing series against Zimbabwe.India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series at home, with their bowlers playing a key role in the campaign. The latest rankings reflect the depth of India’s bowling resources, with Nandani and Kranti rewarded for their performances in the first two matches in Raipur.Nandani emerged as one of the biggest movers, climbing 26 places to 45th in the T20I bowling rankings. The right-arm seamer has claimed three wickets across the first two matches, making her one of the joint-leading wicket-takers in the series.Teammate Kranti also made progress, moving up nine places to 43rd. Their rise adds to the achievements of Charani and Deepti, who remain first and second, respectively, after delivering economical performances against Zimbabwe.Shree Charani, Deepti Sharma maintain their gripCharani continues to lead the T20I bowling rankings, with experienced all-rounder Deepti occupying second place. Their continued presence at the summit underlines India’s strength in the shortest format, where spin has remained a key component of the bowling attack.The latest update also highlights the growing contribution of India’s pace options. Nandani’s 26-place jump and Kranti’s rise of nine positions show how the performances of the supporting bowlers are strengthening the team’s resources ahead of future international assignments.New Zealand bowlers and batters make gainsThere were also changes in the T20I rankings following the opening match of the trans-Tasman series between Australia and New Zealand in Sydney.Australia seamer Annabel Sutherland climbed one place to eighth among T20I bowlers, while New Zealand’s Jess Kerr rose five spots to 17th. Teammates Bree Illing and Nensi Patel also improved, moving up six places to 23rd and five places to 35th, respectively.New Zealand batters Maddy Green and Georgia Plimmer made progress in the T20I batting rankings. Green climbed three places to 34th, while Plimmer made a significant 13-place jump to 48th.Australia’s Beth Mooney, meanwhile, retained her position as the world’s top-ranked T20I batter.Megan Schutt, Ellyse Perry rise in ODI rankingsThe latest update also brought gains for Australian players in the ODI rankings following their 50-over series against Bangladesh in the ICC Women’s Championship.Veteran fast bowler Megan Schutt moved up one place to fourth in the ODI bowling rankings. Ellyse Perry climbed one spot to ninth among ODI batters and made an even bigger jump in the all-rounders’ list, rising 14 places to 25th.Sutherland also benefited from her unbeaten half-century in the final ODI, moving up four places to 13th in the batting rankings.
